commit changed the proof-record COUNT, because the block records one. It does

=== THE GATE REJECTS THIS AGREE, AND I WILL NOT EDIT MY IDENTITY TO FIX IT ===
This is the finding that matters, and it is about the gate, not the branch.
I built a record carrying exactly the identity fields below and ran:
    python scripts/lwb_lanes.py --base bfe8507 --head HEAD --pr-number 38
    FAIL: reviewer_id and commit_author_id share the segment 'buildcraft'
          (10 characters, at or above MIN_SHARED_SEGMENT_LENGTH=8) --
          likely the same session or dispatch reviewing its own work,
          not an independent reviewer
Every "0 independent review(s)" failure remained. So this AGREE does not
count, and lwb-lanes stays red.
The shared segment is THE REPOSITORY'S OWN NAME. It is in my reviewer_id
because the routine that dispatched me mandates the string
"reviewer-cloud-routine-buildcraft" verbatim, and it is in the author id
because the conductor names itself after the repository too. Two identities
that could not be more different in origin — one fired by a clock with no
sight of the other's session — collide on the one word both are obliged to
carry. This is the false positive reviews/README.md predicts in its own
"Known residual" section, and both of #35's reviewers already reported it.
I COULD PASS THE GATE RIGHT NOW by dropping "buildcraft" from my id. I am not
going to. That is relabelling an identifier to make a gate pass, there is a
decision on the books against it, and an id edited to clear a validator is
exactly the falsification pressure the id format was written to remove. A
gate that can only be satisfied by a reviewer willing to misname itself is
worse than no gate.
So the honest state of this PR is: CI green everywhere else, one review gate
red, and the review gate is red for a reason no honest reviewer identity in
this repository can clear. That needs an owner decision or a lwb_lanes.py
fix, and neither is a reviewer's to make — relaxing my own review gate is
precisely what D20 forbids.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS, offered as suggestions and nothing more: exclude the
repository's own name from the segment comparison; or compare only the
parsed session-token segment rather than every segment; or keep the set-based
rule but subtract a small list of segments that carry no identity information
(the repo name, the agent brand). Each has its own failure mode and I have
not measured any of them.

reviewed_commit against resolve_reviewable_head, and those differ here:

I did not resolve that by relabelling. I RAN THE ENTIRE BATTERY ABOVE AT
57f130ab AS WELL, as a separate checkout, and it is green there too. So
naming 57f130ab is a true statement about a commit I actually examined, not a
sha borrowed to satisfy arithmetic. For completeness, the difference between
the two commits is:
    git diff --stat 57f130ab 67e1ea4e  ->  proof/38.json | 6 +++---
three changed lines inside one proof record, and nothing else in the tree.
I examined both. I am recording the one the gate binds to, and telling you
